entries.english:
6 January 1357. Bernhard, son of the late Bohunek von Harach, sells to Abbot Albrecht and the community of Hohenfurt monastery one and a half fiefs at Beichenthal for twenty pounds and sixty Passau pennies. 21 December 1358. Andreas, parish priest at Hoeritz, receives certain meadows and fields from Hohenfurt monastery in return for an annual rent of four shillings of Passau pennies in aid of the Mass.

To all people who see this letter: I, Bernhart, son of the late lord Wohvnken of Harach, make known and openly acknowledge that, with considered judgment, with the consent of my wife Elspet and all my heirs, and with the counsel of my brothers and all my friends, I have sold my one-and-a-half fief at Reychenthal, which was my rightful hereditary property and freehold. At that time Fridereich Pyernheypel was settled on the whole holding, and it renders every year one pound less ten Passau pennies, half at Saint George’s Day and half at Saint Michael’s Day, together with the full tithe and, in place of the other small services—eggs, hens, cutting pennies, and rowolt—forty-one pennies in all. On the half-fief at that time sat Nyclas der Wewer, who renders each year three shillings and fourteen Passau pennies on the same due dates as the aforesaid, with the full tithe, and must pay twenty-two Passau pennies in place of all small services, eggs, hens, cutting pennies, and other dues. I have sold these holdings to the worthy lords, Abbot Albrecht and the entire community of Hohenfurt monastery, for twenty pounds less sixty Passau pennies, which they have paid and delivered to me in full.

I, the aforesaid Bernhart, together with my brothers, have pledged to them on our faith and by this letter that, should any dispute arise in future concerning that hereditary property, whatever its cause, I shall settle and put it right for them without any effort or loss to them, according to the law of the land. Whatever loss they suffer thereby, they shall be entitled to recover from all my hereditary property and freeholds, wherever I have them within or outside the land. So that this agreement may remain wholly firm and unchallenged, I give them this letter sealed with my seal and that of my brother Benesch, and with the seal of my lord, Lord Jost von Rosenberg. This letter was given after the birth of Christ, in the year thirteen hundred and fifty-seven, on the day of Epiphany.

Three small seals hang from parchment strips; the first two are in green wax. (a) A shield bearing three peacock feathers. — S. Pernharti D. Haroch. (b) A shield bearing the same device. Compare XCVI; here the inscription reads: S. Benichs De Harach. (c) The seal of Jodok von Rosenberg, in red wax. Compare CIV and CVIII.

21 December 1358. Andreas, parish priest at Hoeritz, receives certain meadows and fields from Hohenfurt monastery in return for an annual rent of four shillings of Passau pennies in aid of the Mass.

Since deeds and acts performed in time by mortal men are therefore confirmed by authentic and public letters of the faithful, so that the way and opportunity for injury and false accusation may be entirely removed from the malicious and the uninformed, therefore I, Andreas, true and legitimate parish priest of the parish church at Hoerycz, make it openly known to all the faithful through this letter that the venerable and religious lords, the abbot and convent of the monastery at Altovado, out of special friendship and in support of me, have granted and handed over to me, for me to possess and cultivate by usufruct for the term of my life, one meadow and the fields which from of old have belonged and shall belong to the house that the convent holds in its full and peaceful possession at Hoerycz, beside the manor and the parish priest’s glebe, adjoining it to the west. The late Lord Petrus, once parish priest there, had duly and lawfully purchased that house, with all its appurtenances, with his own money for fourteen talents of Passau pennies from the aforesaid convent, solely for his own use. For that house he faithfully paid every year to the custodian’s office at Altovado, at Christmas, a rent of four shillings of Passau pennies. I promise, intend, and am bound to pay that same rent, on the same due date every year, to the aforesaid monastery for the said meadow and fields for as long as I possess them, without negligence or excuse.

The witnesses to this, with their seals attached, are: Lord Petrus von Rosenberg; Lord Bohdancius, dean of Dvdelwiensis; the lord parish priest of Chrvmpnawe; Lord Johannes, parish priest at Rozenberch; and Lord Hainricus, parish priest at Merira. This was given in the year of the Lord 1358, on the feast of Saint Thomas the Apostle.

Six seals hang from parchment strips. Most are poorly impressed but otherwise well preserved, in white wax. (a) Rather large. Saint Katherine. — S. Andre ... De Hoericz. (b) The small seal of Peter von Rosenberg. Compare CIV. (c) Small. Saint Vincent? ... danc ... (d) Fairly large. Saint Vitus; the inscription is illegible. (e) Fairly large. Saint Nicholas. — S. Johan ... lebani enberch. (f) Small. A bird resembling a partridge, with a five-petalled rose before it; the background is filled with small stars. — S. Herici [Pull no?]. De Rosenherch.
